name: nocturne
label: Afterdark
description: True stories of war, spies and assassinations told the way the best 3D history channels tell them: the moments nobody filmed rebuilt in real-time 3D at night — moonlight, haze, silhouettes, FPV drone moves through the clouds and into the scene — cut against short bursts of real black-and-white newsreel on the people and events the narration names. The real photographs lie on a dossier desk under a lamp, a real portrait lights up in a black void, and a negative flash marks every cut between the 3D and the archive. Claude directs every 3D shot from the narration, looks at preview stills of each one and fixes what is wrong before the final render on this computer's graphics card.
tagline: The night nobody filmed, in 3D and archive.
points: Night reconstructions in real-time 3D: moonlight, haze, silhouettes, one light you can explain
FPV drone one-takes — through the clouds, into the bomber, down with the parachutes
Real black-and-white newsreel on the people and events the narration names
Real photographs on a dossier desk and a real portrait in a black void — never a 3D face
Negative-flash cuts between the 3D and the archive, typewriter date strips
Claude directs and checks every shot; renders on your own graphics card
cost: the voice is about $0.05 a minute; the archive film is watched free on the Gemini free tier; Claude's directing runs on your Claude Code plan (a 10-minute video uses about 5 % of a Claude Max 5x week); the 3D renders on this computer, about 10-15 minutes per minute of video

voice.note: Jon, a calm, grounded documentary narrator from the public ElevenLabs library (the 3D channel's voice), so a NOCTURNE video speaks out of the box. Pick another in the app (Voice step) or paste its id here. wavespeed_voice is the voice used when WaveSpeed speaks instead of Algrow.

youtube.brief: Black-and-white newsreel film and archive photographs of the 1930s-1940s (or the story's own era) showing exactly the people, places, institutions and events the narration names: rallies, parades, funerals, troops, officials, streets of the time. No modern footage, no colourised or AI-upscaled copies, no documentary presenters, no burned-in titles or subtitles.
youtube.pick_taste: A clean full-frame shot of the named person or event beats a wide generic one; real movement (marching, a car arriving, a crowd turning) beats a static frame; 1-2 s of the strongest part is enough.

look.options_note: NOCTURNE videos are about two thirds real-time 3D at night; the rest is real black-and-white archive film on the sentences that name real people and events, and maps where the geography matters. The first seconds of the cold open stay 3D. Where the 3D meets the archive Legion cuts with a flash: one punched-in frame and one negative frame. Up to five real photographs of the people the script names (found by PHOTO FX or on Wikimedia Commons) are placed on a dossier desk or lit in a black void: a real face is only ever shown through a real photograph. Claude directs every 3D shot, checks preview frames of each one and fixes what fails before this computer's graphics card renders the final. Keep YouTube footage on (it brings the archive.org films too): with it off the whole video is 3D (no AI pictures). The render farm cannot render 3D: NOCTURNE videos are made on this computer.

prompts.outline:
You are the head writer of a premium history documentary channel whose pictures are real-time 3D reconstructions at night cut against real black-and-white archival film: true stories of war, espionage, assassinations and resistance, told as a story you cannot stop watching.

TITLE: [INSERT TITLE HERE]
LENGTH: [INSERT LENGTH — e.g., 15 minutes, 20 minutes, 25 minutes]

Plan the episode in plain prose, as numbered beats of about one minute each, in causal or chronological order.
- Everything is real: real people, real places, real dates, real numbers. Use only facts you are certain of. Where sources disagree, plan the widely cited round figure with "around", or the range.
- Beat 1 is a cold open in ONE specific, dated moment (the date, the hour, the place) at the most dramatic point of the story — something nobody filmed, so the 3D can show it — then name the person it is all about and pull back to how it came to that.
- Every beat carries two kinds of pictures and names both: the private moments nobody filmed (a room at night, a figure at a window, a car on a dark road, a parachute drop) for the 3D, and the public, documented events of the time (rallies, parades, funerals, troops, officials, newspaper photographs) for the archival film.
- Name the people and say exactly what each of them did and when. Name the institutions and the places.
- Build tension: every few beats a turn, a question the viewer wants answered, and the answer a beat later.
- The last beat lands the consequence as a fact or a number, and returns to the image of the cold open.
For each beat, write the facts it states, the 3D sights that show it, and the archival film or photographs that prove it.
prompts.script:
Write the complete narration for this documentary from the plan below.

THE PLAN:
[INSERT OUTLINE HERE]

HOW IT SOUNDS
- A calm, confident narrator. Short declarative sentences, mostly present tense for the story, past tense for background. Fragments are welcome at turning points: "Two minutes." "Nobody answered."
- The first words are the cold open: the moment, the place, what the people in it are doing — the date itself is shown on screen, so the first sentence can go straight to the people.
- Name real people, places and events in full the first time ("Reinhard Heydrich, the head of the Reich Security Main Office"): those sentences carry the real archival film.
- Every other sentence carries something a camera could film at night: a place, a person doing something, a vehicle, the weather, the light.
- Real facts only. No invented quotes, no invented figures; disputed figures are rounded and said with "around".
- Plain spoken text only: no headings, no stage directions, no speaker labels, no quotation marks around dialogue, no lists, no markdown — no asterisks or underscores for emphasis or a ship's name (write: the ferry Hydro, never *Hydro*): every character you write is burned into the captions.
- Write dates and numbers the way a narrator reads them aloud ("May twenty-seventh, nineteen forty-two"), never digits or symbols.
- Every minute or two, a question the viewer wants answered, answered soon after.
- Never say "in this video". End on the consequence, back at the image of the cold open; then one short line asking viewers to subscribe for the next story.

thumbnail.brief: One cinematic 3D night frame from the story: blue moonlight and haze, a silhouetted figure or vehicle lit by one motivated light, one element in red (a light, a slit across a face in shadow, a flag) — or the real black-and-white portrait of the person as a print lit by a red slit of light. Two to four words of headline in a quiet serif, off-white, with one word in red (#C8322A). No CG faces, no arrows, no stickers, no cartoon.
thumbnail.note: Send Claude five thumbnails you wish were yours and ask it to rewrite this brief.
